title: Config Sentinel: automated evidence collector for regional residency and retention locks
creator: Elena Gomez
description: Build a Config Sentinel service that continuously snapshots compliance-critical configuration (region residency tags, retention TTLs, access policies) and bundles cryptographic evidence for automated audits. The sentinel will run policy-as-code checks, detect config drift across hosted/dedicated/private deployments, and trigger remediation or operator playbooks depending on severity.
motivation: Customers in regulated industries require tamper-evident proof that data residency and retention constraints are enforced. Current drift detection is ad-hoc; we need deterministic evidence artifacts and automated remediation hooks to reduce manual audit overhead and outage risk.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel runs hourly and produces a signed evidence bundle for each account containing: config snapshot, policy evaluation results, and affected resource list
Evidence bundles are stored in an immutable S3 prefix with retention and access logs and appear in Console audit view
When a high-severity drift is detected (residency mismatch or retention TTL < policy), an automated canary remediation is attempted and an incident is opened if remediation fails
Playbooks (per-region) are generated for operator review and include a rollback plan and risk estimate
Unit and e2e tests validate policy-as-code rules against a simulated multi-region inventory
Performance: snapshot + evaluation for 10k resources completes within 6 minutes with <10% additional load on control plane
tasks: Design evidence bundle schema and signing format (Elena)
Implement snapshotting worker and incremental change capture (Marcus)
Write policy-as-code rules for residency and retention (Ravi)
Integrate bundles with console audit store and retention lifecycle (Storage team)
Add remediation runner with dry-run and force modes (Marcus)
Create operator playbook templates and Slack/PagerDuty hooks (Oncall/Support)
End-to-end tests and simulated audit harness (QA)
Performance tuning and kernel selection for large inventories (Infra)
Security review and KMS signing key rotation plan (Security)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Frequent snapshotting increases read volume on control plane; we mitigate by incremental changelog and back-pressure windows
Fully automated remediation reduces time-to-compliance but risks unintended changes; guard with dry-run, approval thresholds, and safe defaults
Evidence immutability requires additional storage costs for long-term retention; propose tiered retention backed by legal requirements
Tight coupling with console audit model may require migration work for older accounts; provide a migration path with compatibility layer
progress_updates: 2025-02-12 - Kickoff: agreed on hourly cadence and signed bundles. Assigned ownership for signing schema to Security.
2025-02-18 - Prototype: snapshot worker implemented against staging inventory; incremental changelog working for 2k resources (Marcus).
2025-02-25 - Policy rules: Ravi authored initial set of CEL rules for residency and TTL thresholds. Found 14 false-positives in test corpus; refined tag-matching heuristics.
2025-03-01 - UI integration: Console audit team exposed /audit/bundles endpoint and mock viewer. Storage lifecycle PR created (PR #5123).
2025-03-04 - Security review requested: key usage pattern documented; pending rotation policy feedback from Security.
decisions_made: Use signed JSON-LD bundles (detached JWS) for evidence to support cross-system verification
Run sentinel in control-plane region with encrypted transit for private deployments; for VPC/on-prem we will ship an agent that posts signed deltas to a customer-owned collector
Automated remediation will be opt-in per-customer and gated by a policy severity matrix; default action is operator-create-incident + suggested remediation
Retention of evidence bundles: 7 years for accounts with compliance tags, 90 days for non-compliant-flag accounts (configurable per-org)
open_questions: Can we leverage existing KV cache to reduce snapshot time or do we need a separate inventory index?
What is the authority model for signing bundles across Dedicated and Private deployments?
Should remediation be synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous with a monitor-and-retry strategy?
review_feedback: PM review (2025-02-20): ask to add a customer-facing remediation opt-in flow in Console
Design review (2025-02-22): suggested evidence viewer should surface diff with previous snapshot and highlight policy lineage
Security review (2025-03-04): recommended HSM-backed signing keys for enterprise customers and an audit of key rotation frequency
related_notes: Investigated drift heuristics vs deterministic enforcement; chose heuristics for tag normalization to reduce false positives
Proof-of-concept showed 40% cost savings when using incremental deltas vs full snapshots for high-change tenants
